content.text: Post B (2206463218284357170) has the lower cost per link click and the higher click-through so far, so I'm shifting the remaining budget toward it. Post A's total goes to $200 (about $4 left after today's spend), and Post B's to $300, so the account total stays at $500.

The campaign ran from Sunday, July 11 through Wednesday, July 15, 2027 (Mountain time), and both line items were set to end at the close of July 15. Total spend was **$490.86** of the $500.00 approved, but one ad group went over its own sub-budget (details below).

**Totals (July 11–15, 2027, all placements, iOS and Android, US and Canada)**

| | Post 2206282024354198610 | Post 2206463218284357170 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $210.92 | $279.94 | $490.86 |
| Impressions | 172,355 | 233,811 | 406,166 |
| Link clicks | 95 | 143 | 238 |

**What these figures show:** X can see impressions, spend and link clicks, and nothing beyond the click. Link clicks are people who tapped through to larchmorrow.com/start. They don't tell us whether anyone started a trial. X has no pixel on your site, so trial starts can only be counted in your own app reporting. Compare the trial-start numbers from your app against the 238 link clicks, and treat the cost per click as a measure of click traffic, not of trials.

**Notes on how I ran it**
- **Structure:** one campaign, "Larchmorrow Summer Strength Trial - Jul 11-15 2027," with one ad group per post. Both ad groups target the United States and Canada, on iOS and Android only.
- **Mid-flight change:** after the first day, Post B had the lower cost per link click ($1.96 versus $2.22 for Post A) and more clicks. On July 15 I moved budget toward it: Post A's total was cut to $200 and its daily to $5, and Post B's total was raised to $300 and its daily to $100.
- **Overspend on Post A:** I set Post A's total to $200 after it had already spent about $196 across the first four days. Its final day ran past that, and Post A finished at $210.92, about $10.92 over its $200 sub-budget. The account total still stays under $500, but the sub-budget was not held as I intended. I should have checked its spend before lowering the cap.
- **Status:** both ad groups carry an end time of the end of July 15 Mountain, so they stop serving then. I didn't pause them manually, and the campaign itself was left active.
- **Posts:** I used only the two approved posts and wrote no new copy.
